description:
FILED s530a (Opus agent, 2026-10-31) while fixing #4000 / #4001.  PRE-EXISTING (base 0fb05a79 gives the same or worse).

A qr// object's class cannot follow perl's REFERENT rule in PCL, because a qr struct (p-regex-match) is SHARED where perl's REGEXP referents are distinct: `qr/$r/` hands back $r's own struct, and two qr/$s/ sites with the same pattern text answer the same struct.  So the class stays on the BOX (the #4001 arm in p-aref-unbox-elem keeps a classed regex box), and the referent-keyed shape #4000 used for ARRAY / CODE / handle / glob (*p-referent-stash*) was tried for qr and REVERTED: it made `ref qr/$r/` answer $r's class.

REPRO (scratch/s530a/pr/b5.pl + b4.pl row 9, perl 5.40.3 vs the s530a tree):
    my $r = bless qr/x/, 'K'; my $r3 = $r; bless $r, 'L'; print ref($r3), "\n";   # perl L, PCL K
    my @l = ($r); bless $r, 'M'; print ref($l[0]), "\n";                          # perl M, PCL L
    my $u = qr/u/; my $u2 = $u; bless $u, 'K'; print ref($u2), "\n";               # perl K, PCL Regexp
    my %h = (k => qr/h/); bless $h{k}, 'K'; print ref($h{k}), "\n";                # perl K, PCL Regexp
    my @a; push @a, qr/z/ for 1..2; bless $a[0], 'K'; print ref($a[0]), "\n";     # perl K, PCL Regexp
  The must-stay rows: `my $r2 = qr/$r/` is `Regexp` in perl (a NEW object), and so is a second qr/$s/.

MECHANISM: (1) bless of an element or hash value whose payload is a RAW qr struct: p-bless gets the raw struct (no box to stamp) and returns a new box nobody stores.  (2) re-bless through a copy: the class lives on each copy's box.  The fix needs qr IDENTITY first: every qr// evaluation (and qr/$r/) must produce a distinct referent object (a thin wrapper around the shared compiled pattern), after which the #4000 referent stash applies unchanged.  Cheap discriminating measurement: `my $a = qr/$s/; my $b = qr/$s/; print refaddr($a) == refaddr($b)` -- perl 0, PCL today: run it.

MEASURED (s530a, scratch/s530a/pr/q1.pl): `qr/$s/` twice -> PCL `same` refaddr (perl distinct); `qr/$a/` with $a a qr -> PCL same (perl distinct); `push @q, qr/z/` twice (one site, constant pattern) -> distinct in both.  So the sharing is the INTERPOLATED qr path (%p-regex-parts / %p-qr-parts handing back a cached or the operand's struct), not the literal one.
subject: a qr// object is SHARED where perl makes distinct REGEXP referents (qr/$r/ returns $r, two qr/$s/ the same struct), so a re-bless through a copy or a bless of a raw qr element / hash value is lost -- silent wrong
